summary: Specifies requirements for solutions supporting MPLS Network Actions (MNAs), which affect forwarding or other processing of MPLS packets. They are informed by proposals to add information to labeled packets so transit or terminating routers can perform actions.

eli5.summary: Packages could carry extra instructions for mail sorters. This lists what a good system for such instructions must do.

questions: what is an mpls network action
what is a network action indicator
subtitle: The checklist any MPLS 'network action' design has to satisfy before routers can act on extra instructions in a packet.

tldr.problem: MPLS routers normally forward on the top label and Traffic Class bits. New use cases want routers to act on more information carried in the labeled packet, and without shared rules the proposals could be incompatible and heavy to implement.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists 55 numbered requirements for solutions that carry Network Action Indicators and ancillary data in or after the label stack, covering general design, the alert mechanism, actions, indicators and ancillary data.
tldr.outcome: It is a requirements document, not a protocol. Later solution specifications are expected to meet these requirements and to address their own security considerations.

today: RFC 9613 is an Informational document and has not been obsoleted or updated. It sets requirements rather than defining a protocol, so the actual MNA solutions are specified elsewhere.

sections.title: Why MPLS Needs Network Actions
sections.content:
MPLS routers (Label Switching Routers, LSRs) classically forward a packet using its top label and Traffic Class (TC) bits. New use cases call for a general mechanism, the MPLS Network Action (MNA), that lets the network decide how to forward or process a packet using other information as well.

The RFC says the extensions must conform to the existing MPLS architecture in RFC 3031, RFC 3032 and RFC 6790. It expects two kinds of follow-on documents: an MNA solution specification describing a common protocol for all MNAs, and Network Action solution specifications that extend it for individual use cases.
sections.eli5: Mail sorters usually look only at the top address on a package. Some jobs need them to read extra notes too, so people want rules for how those notes should work.

sections.title: The Vocabulary of MNA
sections.content:
A Network Action (NA) is an operation performed on an MPLS packet, or as a result of processing one. A Network Action Indicator (NAI) is the marking in the packet that says a certain NA is to be performed. Ancillary Data (AD) is data tied to an NA that can be input to the action or a result of it.

AD comes in two placements. In-Stack Data sits inside the MPLS label stack. Post-Stack Data sits between the bottom of the label stack and the first octet of the user payload. A Scope is the set of nodes that should perform a given action.
sections.eli5: The action is the job, the indicator is the sticker saying which job, and the ancillary data is the note stuck on with details. The note can go on the label itself or underneath it.

sections.title: General Requirements
sections.content:
The first fifteen requirements set the ground rules. Solutions MUST keep the extensibility, flexibility and efficiency of MPLS's split between a control plane and a simple data plane, MUST NOT restrict the generality of the MPLS architecture, and MUST coexist with existing MPLS mechanisms. They MAY carry MNA information in-stack, post-stack or both, but implementations are not forced to support in-stack or post-stack data unless they choose an NA that uses it.

They MUST minimize the processing needed to parse the label stack and MUST minimize additions to its size. Specifications MUST discuss ECMP consequences, and MUST discuss any growth of the label stack that the ingress router does not control. Packets with NAIs MUST be able to share an LSP with packets that have none.

Requirement 12 says a Network Action solution MUST NOT expose information to LSRs that is not already exposed to the LER (the Label Edge Router at the network edge).
sections.eli5: The new system must fit the old one, stay fast, not make the label bigger than it has to be, and work on the same road as packets that have no extra notes.

sections.title: Alerts, Actions and Indicators
sections.content:
An MNA solution MUST define how a node can tell whether NAIs are present. Special Purpose Labels are called a mechanism of last resort, so any design that uses them MUST minimize how many new ones it allocates.

For actions, it is RECOMMENDED that a solution support NAs for Private Use. A specification MUST say whether an NA must be handled as part of the immediate forwarding operation and whether packet misordering may result, and must define precedence if an NA allows more than one scope.

For indicators, an NAI MUST NOT be imposed for a node unless that node is known to support it, and the control and management planes MUST be able to learn whether downstream LSRs can handle a given NAI. Several NAIs MUST be allowed in one packet, and an implementation is not required to process all of them. NAIs MUST only be inserted by LSRs that push a label, such as head-end LSRs and points of local repair.
sections.eli5: Nobody should stick a special instruction on a package unless the sorter down the line can read it. Several stickers may be on one package, and a sorter may ignore ones it does not know.

sections.title: Ancillary Data Rules
sections.content:
Specifications MUST say whether a given action needs ancillary data and whether it is in-stack, post-stack or both, and whether an LSR may rewrite it. Quantities of in-stack data MUST be limited to the minimum needed, and post-stack data SHOULD NOT be used unless the size of the data could stop the action coexisting with other MPLS functions if placed in the stack.

The structure of an NAI and its data MUST allow unknown NAIs and their data to be skipped. Removing an NAI MUST also remove its ancillary data unless remaining NAIs need it. A mechanism MUST exist to tell the egress LER that ancillary data is present. Not more than one Standards Track solution SHOULD be defined for encoding in-stack data, and likewise for post-stack data.
sections.eli5: Keep the notes short, put them on the label only when they fit, let sorters skip notes they cannot read, and tell the last sorter to remove any leftover notes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
MPLS forwarding on its own has no built-in security mechanisms. The RFC warns that solutions may embed information derived from the MPLS payload in the MPLS headers, which could expose data the user assumed was opaque to the network.

An LSR that changes forwarding based on inserted data creates an implicit trust relationship with the upstream LSR that inserted it. Each solution specification MUST address the security considerations its design introduces, and should be read together with the MNA framework document.
sections.eli5: Notes added to a package must not leak what is inside, and a sorter that trusts another sorter's note should know it is doing so.
